newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH JAN-APR OIL PRODUCTS SALES FALL 5 PCT Y/Y.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH JAN-APR OIL PRODUCTS SALES FALL 5 PCT Y/Y.

text.p: Sales in Finland of oil products fell five percent year-on-year in January-April to about 2.80 million tonnes, the Finnish Petroleum Association said in its monthly review received on Friday.
January-April sales of industrial heating oil fell 15 percent year-on-year to 488,074 tonnes, while sales of domestic heating oil fell 10 percent to 778,558 tonnes, it said.
Four-month sales of motor petroleum rose four percent year-on-year to 566,687 tonnes, and diesel sales rose seven percent to 510,228 tonnes, the association said.
Sales of other oil products fell six percent to 459,580 tonnes, it said.
Total domestic sales of all categories of oil products this year are expected to fall by more than two percent and to grow next year by about one percent, the association said.
Although mild weather early in 1997 had hit demand for heating oil, economic growth would probably increase sales of oil products during the two-year forecast period, it said.
Finnish oil consumption is expected to fall this year by about 1.5 percent and to grow by the same ratio next year, it said.

Motor petroleum consumption is expected to remain stable this year and next at about the same level as in 1996, while diesel sales are expected to rise about three percent this year and about 1.5 percent next year, it said.
Sales of light heating oil would fall three percent this year on last year, and would remain stable next year, it said.
Sales of industrial heating oil are seen falling nine percent this year and by about 1.5 percent next year, the association said.
World crude oil prices have fallen this spring from the peak end-year level, the association's managing director Jaakko Tusa said in the review.
And though crude prices look set to seesaw in the near-term, no longer-term price pressures up or down are apparent, Tusa said.

The profitability of the European oil refining industry has generally been unsatisfactory in recent years, and overcapacity is expected to prevent significant improvement in profitability in the next few years, the association said.
